record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: dynamical degrees as weak Perron numbers
record.original_question: Is the dynamical degree of every polynomial automorphism of C^d a weak Perron number of algebraic degree at most d−1?

evidence.quote: Question 38. — Is the dynamical degree of any polynomial automorphism of Cd equal to a weak Perron number of degree ≤ d − 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \colon \mathbb{C}^d \to \mathbb{C}^d$ be a polynomial automorphism, i.e., a bijective polynomial map whose inverse is also polynomial. The (first) dynamical degree of $f$ is defined by
$$\lambda_1(f) \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \bigl(\deg(f^n)\bigr)^{1/n},$$
where $\deg$ denotes the maximum of the degrees of the coordinate components. A real algebraic integer $\lambda \geq 1$ is called a weak Perron number if $\lambda \geq |\lambda'|$ for every Galois conjugate $\lambda'$ of $\lambda$. Its algebraic degree is the degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Question: Is it true that for every $d \geq 2$ and every polynomial automorphism $f$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$, the dynamical degree $\lambda_1(f)$ is a weak Perron number whose algebraic degree is at most $d-1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on Hénon-type and polynomial automorphism dynamics. Partial progress exists: for affine-triangular automorphisms of affine spaces it is known that every weak Perron number arises as a dynamical degree, and the converse direction (dynamical degrees are weak Perron) is known in various special classes (e.g., surfaces, abelian varieties). No general proof or counterexample for all polynomial automorphisms of $\mathbb{C}^d$ in arbitrary dimension has been located, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical degrees of affine-triangular automorphisms of affine spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Each weak Perron number is the dynamical degree of an affine-triangular automorphism of the affine space C^n for some n.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that weak Perron numbers do arise as dynamical degrees of polynomial automorphisms (one direction), but does not prove the converse in general dimension.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical degrees of birational transformations of projective surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of which algebraic numbers occur as dynamical degrees of birational surface maps.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the surface (d=2) case results consistent with the weak Perron property, but the higher-dimensional question remains.
